subject: Physical Education
name: Physical Education, Units 3 and 4
about: VCE, Skills, energy systems and training
syllabus: VCE Physical Education Study Design (from 2025), Units 3 and 4

units.title: Unit 3: Movement skills and energy for physical activity, sport and exercise

points.title: Classifying movement skills
points.brief: Skills can be classed as fundamental or sport-specific, gross or fine, open or closed, and discrete, serial or continuous.

points.title: Skills, participation and performance
points.brief: Developing motor skills makes people more likely to take part and to perform well.

points.title: Sociocultural factors in skill learning
points.brief: Family, peers, culture, access to facilities and coaching all affect how skills develop.

points.title: Stages of learning
points.brief: Learners move from the cognitive stage (thinking through each step), to the associative stage (refining), to the autonomous stage (automatic).

points.title: Direct and constraints-led coaching
points.brief: Linear theories suit direct coaching that breaks skills into steps; non-linear theories suit a constraints-led approach that shapes tasks and environments.

points.title: Psychological skills
points.brief: Confidence, motivation, the right level of arousal and concentration, with strategies such as imagery and self-talk, help performance.

points.title: Practice schedules
points.brief: Practice can be massed or distributed, and blocked or random, each suiting different skills and stages of learning.

points.title: Feedback
points.brief: Feedback can be internal or external, and about the result or the movement itself. Too much can make a learner depend on it.

points.title: Linear and angular motion
points.brief: Force and torque, momentum, impulse, and speed and velocity describe how bodies move in straight lines and rotate.

points.title: Newton's laws of motion
points.brief: Inertia, acceleration in proportion to force, and equal and opposite reactions explain how athletes and objects move.

points.title: Projectile motion
points.brief: The release height, speed and angle decide how far and how high an object or body flies.

points.title: Levers in the body
points.brief: Most body movements use third-class levers, which trade force for speed. Axis, force and resistance set the mechanical advantage.

points.title: Balance and stability
points.brief: A lower centre of gravity, a wider base of support and the line of gravity inside the base make a body more stable.

points.title: Qualitative movement analysis
points.brief: Coaches prepare, observe, evaluate and correct errors to improve a movement.

points.title: ATP and energy for movement
points.brief: Muscles need ATP to contract. The body stores very little, so it must be rebuilt constantly by three energy systems.

points.title: The ATP-PC system
points.brief: Uses phosphocreatine to rebuild ATP very fast, for about 10 seconds of maximal effort such as a sprint start.

points.title: The anaerobic glycolysis system
points.brief: Breaks down glucose without oxygen for high-intensity efforts lasting up to about a minute, producing hydrogen ions that bring fatigue.

points.title: The aerobic system
points.brief: Breaks down carbohydrate and fat with oxygen to make a large amount of ATP slowly, for longer, lower-intensity activity.

points.title: The energy systems working together
points.brief: All three systems work at once, but the main one depends on how hard and how long the effort is.

points.title: Oxygen uptake
points.brief: At the start of exercise oxygen supply lags (oxygen deficit), then levels off (steady state), and stays high after (EPOC) as the body recovers.

points.title: Acute responses in Unit 3
points.brief: During exercise the cardiovascular, respiratory and muscular systems respond together to supply energy.

points.title: Fatigue
points.brief: Fatigue comes from running out of fuel, a build-up of metabolic by-products, and overheating, depending on intensity and duration.

points.title: Nutrition and hydration for performance
points.brief: Carbohydrate, protein and water before, during and after exercise improve performance, delay fatigue and help recovery.

chapters.title: Foundations of an effective training program

points.title: Activity analysis
points.brief: Watching an activity to find its movement skills, energy systems, muscles and fitness components, so training can match it.

points.title: Fitness components
points.brief: Aerobic power, anaerobic capacity, muscular strength, power, endurance, speed, agility, flexibility and body composition.

points.title: Fitness testing
points.brief: Fitness tests find strengths and weaknesses, set goals and motivate. Standard, recognised tests should match what the activity needs.

points.title: Before testing
points.brief: Health screening and informed consent come before any fitness test.

points.title: Test reliability, validity and accuracy
points.brief: A good fitness test gives consistent results, measures the right component and is close to the true value.

points.title: Monitoring training
points.brief: Training diaries, heart rate and ratings of perceived exertion track whether training is working and how hard it is.

points.title: A training session
points.brief: Each session has a warm up, a conditioning phase and a cool down.

points.title: Principles of training
points.brief: Frequency, intensity, time, type, specificity, progressive overload, variety and individuality guide a program.

points.title: Detraining and plateaus
points.brief: Fitness gains are lost when training stops (detraining), and progress can stall without changes to the program.

points.title: Training methods
points.brief: Continuous, interval, fartlek, circuit, resistance, plyometric and flexibility training each build particular fitness components.

points.title: Chronic cardiovascular adaptations
points.brief: Months of aerobic training enlarge the heart, raise stroke volume and lower resting heart rate.

points.title: Chronic respiratory adaptations
points.brief: Aerobic training makes breathing more efficient and lifts VO2 max.

points.title: Chronic muscular adaptations
points.brief: Resistance training grows muscle fibres (hypertrophy) and improves the nerves' control of them.

points.title: What adaptations improve
points.brief: Training adaptations lift VO2 max, raise the lactate inflection point, speed up and strengthen muscle contractions and improve lactate tolerance.

points.title: Skill, biomechanics and energy together
points.brief: Improving performance means linking how a skill is learned, how it is performed and the energy and fitness it needs.

points.title: Designing a program for an athlete
points.brief: A good program matches the activity analysis, the athlete's test results and the training principles, and changes as they improve.
